sections.title: Grammar bridge
sections.description: Master the structures that connect this B1 module to the next stage.

points.title: Advice and obligation
points.function: Use should for advice, must for strong rules, and have to for external requirements.
examples: I have to submit this today.

points.title: First conditional
points.function: Use if + present, will + verb for a likely future result.
examples: If you leave now, you will arrive on time.
Unless you hurry, you will miss it.

points.title: Second conditional
points.function: Use if + past, would + verb for an imaginary situation.
examples: If I had more time, I would exercise more.
What would you do if you lost your phone?

tip.title: Accuracy first
tip.text: Notice the verb form in every example, then change the subject or time expression to make a new sentence.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.description: Choose the best answer, then read the explanation.

questions.prompt: Your doctor has advised you not to ignore the pain. If it continues for another two days, you ___ make an appointment.
questions.explanation: Should gives advice. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: Employees ___ wear an ID card; it is company policy.
questions.explanation: Have to expresses an external rule. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: If it rains, we ___ the event indoors.
questions.explanation: First conditional uses will in the result.

questions.prompt: Unless you ___ now, you will be late.
questions.explanation: After unless, use the present simple. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: If I knew the answer, I ___ tell you.
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses would + verb. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: Take some cash ___ the card machine is broken.
questions.explanation: In case prepares for a possible problem.

tip.title: Use the clue
tip.text: Look for time expressions, the subject, and words before or after the gap before choosing.

sections.title: Listening: Asking for Study Advice
sections.description: Listen to a caller describe a problem and an adviser suggest practical solutions.

audio.transcript: I've recently started an evening course, but I'm struggling to keep up. I work full time, and by the time I get home, I'm often too tired to study. If I leave everything until the weekend, I feel overwhelmed. What should I do? First, you should make the task smaller. If you study for twenty minutes each weekday, you won't have so much work left on Saturday. You could also use your journey to review vocabulary. Most importantly, speak to your teacher. If they know about your schedule, they may help you choose the most important exercises. You shouldn't aim for a perfect routine immediately. Try the new plan for two weeks, and then adjust it according to what actually works.

gistQuestions.prompt: What problem does the caller have?
options: There is not enough time and energy to study
gistQuestions.explanation: The caller works full time and feels too tired to keep up.

detailQuestions.prompt: What does the adviser suggest doing during the journey?
detailQuestions.explanation: The journey can be used to review vocabulary.

detailQuestions.prompt: How long should the caller test the new plan?
detailQuestions.explanation: The adviser recommends trying it for two weeks.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Separate the caller's problem from the adviser's suggestions and conditional consequences.

sections.title: Build a spoken answer
sections.description: Answer each question aloud. Aim for a clear answer plus one reason or detail.
questions: What advice would you give a stressed student?
What rules are important at work or school?
What would you change if you had more free time?
sections.sampleAnswer: A stressed student should make a simple study plan and take regular breaks. If they sleep well, they will concentrate better. I would also recommend asking for help.

tip.title: Speak in layers
tip.text: Start with a direct answer, add a reason, then give one example or detail.

sections.title: Independent writing
sections.description: Reply to a friend who is struggling to study and work at the same time.

prompt.situation: Give practical advice, explain one obligation, and use both a first and second conditional.
prompt.referenceAnswer: A stressed student should make a simple study plan and take regular breaks. If they sleep well, they will concentrate better. I would also recommend asking for help.

tip.title: Final check
tip.text: Check verb forms, word order, spelling, and whether every sentence helps answer the task.
